subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic -> open models (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rivera <emily@acmehealth.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic -> open models (Acme Health)

Hi Emily / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call to confirm I captured your pain, goals, and next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points & goals
- Cost: OpenAI/Anthropic spend has become a top-3 operational line item for your consumer chat product. You want predictable unit economics and a path to lower per-token costs.
- Vendor lock & control: Risk from single-provider API dependencies and data governance for PHI-adjacent usage.
- Latency & reliability: Must meet 95th percentile latency targets for peak traffic; can’t degrade user experience during outages.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Frontend/Prod: Customer-facing chat built on next.js, calls to backend microservices.
- Model usage: OpenAI (gpt-4o) for generation, Anthropic Claude-instant for safety/reranking in some flows.
- Orchestration: Homegrown request router, SSO via Okta, logs shipped to Splunk.

Success criteria for migration
- Equivalent or better answer quality (production evals on 10k prompt set)
- <20% higher 95th latency vs current for initial rollout (target: within 150ms of current SLA)
- >=30% reduction in per-token inference cost after steady-state (w/ batching & quantization)
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence + optional VPC/private deployment for PHI workloads

Compatibility & shortlist (initial)
- Requirements: OpenAI/Anthropic API compatibility layer (request/response shape, function calls), instruction-tuned open models, multi-precision/quantization support.
- Shortlist: Llama-2-Chat / Llama-3 variants (quantized), Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-180B-Instruct, and Mosaic/Redwood-verified smaller models for embedding/rerank. See attached model-shortlist.csv for mapping to your current prompts.

Proposed next steps
1) Tech kickoff: 60–90 minute technical deep-dive with your infra and security (please include procurement and engineering leads).
2) Mutual Action Plan (MAP): I attached an initial MAP and a HubSpot link. We propose a 3-phase PoC: discovery -> PoC (integrate model + evaluate) -> pilot (traffic split).
3) Security questionnaire: You flagged SOC 2 and data residency—I'll loop in our security team and attach the baseline docs.
4) Pricing & procurement: After PoC sizing, we'll surface Dedicated and Private options + estimated reserved capacity impact.

Attachments: redwood-migration-MAP.pdf, model-shortlist.csv

Proposed times for kickoff: Tue 12/1 10:00–11:30 PT, Wed 12/2 14:00–15:30 PT — let me know what works.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference for teams

Neha —

Thanks for the thorough recap — that matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications and asks before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Security/compliance: We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short inventory of audit logs and KMS integrations. Can you confirm Redwood can provide that (or share existing docs)?
2) Latency expectations: The 95th pct target you noted — can you share baseline numbers we should expect for the shortlist models on p95 for 1k token requests? Our SRE (Tom) will evaluate against our SLA.
3) Procurement: Adding procurement on cc — we’ll need a ballpark pricing model for PoC vs pilot vs production (monthly committed vs pay-as-you-go).

I’ve attached our security intake and a short questionnaire — happy to fill more if needed.

Also we prefer Tue 12/1 10:00 PT for the kickoff.

Best,

Hi Emily / Tom / procurement —

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround and for confirming Tue 12/1 10:00 PT. See answers inline to your asks and next steps below.

Security/compliance
- SOC 2: Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. We also offer Private deployment (VPC) and HSM/KMS integrations for PHI workflows. I'll have our security lead share a summary pack before the kickoff.
- Audit logs: We expose per-request tracing and token-level usage logs; logs can be forwarded to your Splunk or pulled from our log export.

Latency baselines (p95)
- Estimated p95 (1k token request) on standard Dedicated infra (NVIDIA H100 equivalent): Llama-3-Chat (quantized FP16) ~ 220–300ms; Mistral-Instruct ~ 200–280ms; Falcon-180B-Instruct (sharded) ~ 300–420ms. These are estimates — we'll validate during PoC.

Pricing & procurement
- PoC pricing: small reserved pool + usage overage; we provide trial credits for evaluation. Pilot/Production: options include Reserved (monthly commit) or pay-as-you-go. I attached an initial MAP with pricing bands.

Next steps (confirmed)
1) Kickoff — Tue 12/1 10:00–11:30 PT (invite to follow). Please include engineering, SRE (Tom), and procurement.
2) Security pack — Redwood security summary + SOC 2 (we'll request NDA).
3) PoC plan — technical milestones in MAP: dataset evals, latency/cost benchmarks, quality gate for rollout.

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
